links.comparator_used: Pre-AI (unexposed) period at the same stroke centers, before alerts were activated; images were analyzed but no alerts, mobile PACS or secure messaging were available
links.outcome: Door-to-groin (DTG) time (primary); CT initiation to EVT start (secondary)
links.effect: DTG reduced by 11.2 min (95% CI -18.22 to -4.2); CT initiation to EVT start reduced by 9.8 min (95% CI -16.9 to -2.6). No difference in IV tPA times (-3.5 min, 95% CI -9.1 to 2.2), length of stay (-0.4 d), or 90-day functional independence (OR 1.3, 95% CI 0.42-4.0).
links.quote: In mixed-effects linear regression, implementation of the LVO detection AI algorithm resulted in a reduction in DTG time by 11.2 minutes.

links.comparator_used: Pre-AI/unexposed standard stroke workflow before site activation; the LVO alerts were not sent and the mobile PACS and patient-level secure messaging were not available.
links.outcome: Door-to-groin time and CT initiation-to-EVT start time for LVO stroke patients treated with EVT
links.effect: Mixed-effects regression: DTG time −11.2 minutes (95% CI, −18.22 to −4.2; P < .01); initiation of CT scan to EVT start time −9.8 minutes (95% CI, −16.9 to −2.6; P < .01). Univariable medians: DTG 100 (IQR, 81-116) minutes pre-AI vs 88 (IQR, 65-110) minutes post-AI; CT-to-EVT 85 (IQR, 68-99) minutes pre-AI vs 72 (IQR, 55-90) minutes post-AI.
links.tradeoff: Total processing time after image acquisition including transmission and software analysis was less than 5 minutes on average; clinical care team had to download the mobile app and sites received onboarding/education.
links.quote: In mixed-effects linear regression, implementation of the LVO detection AI algorithm resulted in a reduction in DTG time by 11.2 minutes.

design_hint: AI LVO detection with real-time mobile alerts to clinicians (stepped-wedge activation)
